Whisky Monster’s 2020 batch-31 review provides a matched sensory record; the later brand range does not silently supersede that bottle.
editorial.production: Published specifications describe a rye-dominant mash with a small barley component, at least two years in oak, and 45.5% ABV. Whisky Monster reports used bourbon barrels with fresh-cut oak staves. The label category is preserved as whiskey distilled from a rye mash; it is not assumed to satisfy American straight-rye new-charred-oak requirements.
editorial.short_version: A sweet, floral legacy rye-mash whiskey with a useful cocktail case. Its used-oak process and label identity deserve their own treatment rather than a straight-rye assumption.

review_evidence.summary: Beiter finds light fruit and honey at the start, balanced apricot/caramel sweetness in the middle and a more satisfying spiced-pastry ending. He regards it as accessible rather than a forceful showcase of heirloom grain.

production_summary: The authenticated launch identity is a blend of straight bourbons distilled by Widow Jane in Brooklyn and sourced from Kentucky. The producer reports four-to-six-year components, while the bottle is NAS. It is non-chill filtered and bottled at 45.5% ABV. Full blend proportions and mash percentages are undisclosed.
history: The nationally distributed 2024 Baby Jane uses the proprietary corn descended from Bloody Butcher and Wapsie Valley. This follows earlier experimental heirloom and very young Baby Jane releases, rather than marking the first time Widow Jane ever distilled bourbon.
The modern bottling combines Brooklyn and Kentucky whiskey. The name’s agricultural story does not authenticate an undisclosed blend proportion or a numerical mash bill for the whole blend.

serving.name: Rocks / water

serving.name: Old Fashioned

serving.name: Manhattan
serving.recommendation: Treat this as a small comparative tasting rather than assuming one-year distillate will carry a full vermouth measure.

editorial.grain: Reported 2016 recipe: 80% Baby Jane corn, 10% rye, 10% malted barley.
editorial.quality_rationale: Rounded sweetness and low harshness are notable for its age, but grain-led youth and a modest finish keep it near competent-to-good on the full Bourbon scale. Age-relative surprise is not reference-class quality.
editorial.value_rationale: The original USD 140 / 375 mL equals USD 280 / 750 mL. That cost is dramatically above capable everyday bourbon; historical interest is excluded from drinking Value, matching the reviewers’ price reservations.
editorial.evidence_limit: Two contributors at one outlet provide one publisher’s matched record. A surprising one-year sample is not proof that later, older Baby Jane is the same whiskey.

pricing.basis: Bourbon & Banter published original 375 mL reference; historical, not current retail
pricing.nc_status: No current NC listing authenticated for this 75-bottle 2016 release. The modern Baby Jane NC price is a different expression.
